experiments.title: October 30 Des Moines temperature: a frozen paper forecast
experiments.hypothesis: Does the issued NWS hourly grid forecast outperform a current-temperature persistence baseline for one future airport-temperature event? This checks a forecasting workflow, not an investment signal.
experiments.nextAction: After October 30, 2026 at 22:15 UTC, retrieve and preserve the qualifying KDSM observation, resolve both frozen forecasts against the same event, and compare Brier and absolute-temperature errors. No automatic collection or trading is scheduled.

findings.summary: Recorded locally at 2026-10-29T21:48:45.429293+00:00. Target: October 30, 2026 at 22:00 UTC. Event: KDSM air temperature is at least 15°C. Outcome remains unresolved; no score or forecast skill is established.

NWS hourly grid: 58°F (14.4444°C), exceedance probability 42.6542%. Persistence: latest received KDSM observation 19°C, exceedance probability 90.8789%. Both probabilities use the same arbitrary normal residual assumption with 3°C standard deviation; they are uncalibrated, not official NWS temperature probabilities.

Use the nearest verified-quality KDSM air-temperature observation within 15 minutes of 22:00 UTC, choosing the earlier observation on a tie. Conflicting or missing observations leave the event unresolved. Both forecasts share the same fixed event definition and outcome.

Original response bytes, SHA-256 and HTTP receipt metadata were retained locally before the decision. Available-at conservatively uses local receipt time; first public dissemination and an independent attestation of the local clock are not established. Forecast source is the DMX grid point; outcome is KDSM station, so spatial mismatch remains.

One event cannot establish calibration or superiority. No commodity, equity or option returns, execution prices, investment profit or trading action are part of this study. This publication is a static reviewed snapshot, not a live outcome feed.

experiments.title: Corn weather outlooks: a negative monthly test
experiments.hypothesis: Do issued summer heat and dryness outlooks improve prediction of monthly corn cash-price changes beyond seasonality and momentum?
experiments.nextAction: Retain the negative result. Test crop-weighted operational forecast revisions against a wholly future outcome only after timing and coverage are resolved.

findings.summary: On 15 evaluation months in 2020-2024, baseline MAE was 8.3764 log percentage points; adding weather worsened it to 8.4623. A zero-change baseline was better than both at 8.2709.

Training used 30 months in 2010-2019. Six-state categorical outlooks were equally weighted, not acreage weighted. The price target partly elapsed before the forecast; cash prices are revised current vintages, not futures returns. Earlier exposure to some data means this is chronological evaluation, not untouched confirmation.

experiments.title: Issued GFS forecasts versus temperature persistence
experiments.hypothesis: Can archived operational GFS temperature forecasts beat a simple persistence forecast for a future observation in a fixed Iowa sample?
experiments.nextAction: Expand weather verification separately from financial testing; do not infer commodity alpha from temperature accuracy.

findings.summary: Across 16 fixed July cases in 2021-2024, GFS MAE was 2.0967 C versus persistence 2.4688 C (15.1% lower). GFS won only 7 of 16 cases and was worse in 2022; mean bias was -1.8181 C.

One airport and four summers. Decision assumed initialization plus 24 hours, with temperature target 60 hours later. Archive timestamps support that lag but do not independently prove earliest public dissemination. Observations are later quality-controlled. This tests weather accuracy, not crop yields, commodity prices or trading profit.

experiments.title: Natural gas and downstream producer prices
experiments.hypothesis: Do lagged natural-gas price changes add predictive information for fertilizer and electric-power producer prices beyond simple controls?
experiments.nextAction: Obtain real-time vintages and test stability before considering any investment signal.

findings.summary: Training: 120 months in 2010-2019; evaluation: 72 months in 2020-2025. Fertilizer MAE improved from 3.3331 to 3.2647 log percentage points (2.05%), but worsened in four of six years. Power MAE worsened from 0.9079 to 0.9099.

Current revised EIA/BLS vintages and an assumed two-month release buffer; no verified point-in-time panel. Producer-price indexes measure neither company margins nor investable returns. These are unstable associations, not causal or profit evidence.

experiments.title: Bird flu and Cal-Maine: the margin bridge
experiments.hypothesis: Can outbreak timing, egg selling prices and feed costs explain the issuer accounting before testing any predictive investment claim?
experiments.nextAction: Build a predefined dated outbreak cohort with earnings overlaps and peer comparisons before testing returns.

findings.summary: FY2024 Q3 versus FY2023 Q3: gross margin fell from 46.419% to 31.088% (-15.331 percentage points). Sold dozens rose while average selling price fell from $3.298 to $2.247 per dozen. Lower feed cost alone did not imply higher margins.

Feed cost uses dozens produced; selling price uses dozens sold. Those denominators cannot be directly subtracted as an egg-margin measure. Kansas outbreak was within the quarter; the April 1 Texas outbreak followed the March 2 quarter end. Independently recomputed descriptive accounting; no event-return or predictive result.

experiments.title: Nursing-home penalties: a public-timing veto
experiments.hypothesis: Could payment denials at competitors redirect admissions to nearby unpenalized operators before that effect is priced?
experiments.nextAction: Require verifiably earlier enforcement publication and historical facility exposure before testing this mechanism.

findings.summary: Across February and March 2024 snapshots, all 277 newly appearing denial intervals had already ended before the snapshot date (median 98 days earlier). January is left-censored. Snapshot dates are not proven first-public dates.

Earlier state suspension notices were found but do not establish first-public federal denial timing. Ownership aliases and available-bed/referral data remain incomplete. No referral effect or stock-return test was run.

findings.summary: All 15 raw brand-change candidates in the screened 68-district subset were audited: ten compared different equipment categories, four were aliases or the same product family, and one remained a different-brand purchase lead.

experiments.title: Location demand: geographic baselines before an LSTM

experiments.nextAction: Supply verified point-in-time location/traffic labels and historical comparable-store membership; run persistence, seasonal and fixed-ridge baselines first. No LSTM is fitted or feed purchased.

findings.summary: Starbucks is an example, not a selected trade. Public comparable transactions are aggregate quarterly growth, not historical store-level demand labels. No licensed traffic feed, historical membership panel or store-level labels verified or acquired.

Freeze historical stores/geofences, opening/closure dates and comparable-store membership. Separate local demand from shifts among nearby stores and net expansion; vendor backfills with newer POIs are not as-delivered historical vintages.

Start fixed geographic exposure, seasonality/no-change and regularized linear baselines. Block geography and chronological holdouts; model/scaler/training-data hashes and availability cutoffs. A multi-horizon LSTM only after sufficient independent labels/coverage; quarterly aggregate labels limit effective sample and store inference.

Python persistence, same-month seasonal and fixed-ridge linear baselines enforce independent feature/label availability, historical feature-decision checks, training-only scaling and separate fixture/real evidence. Tests use synthetic data only. No real store-level demand labels or model performance.
